literal.prompt: Какая охраняемая территория особенно известна европейским зубром?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The stem’s key association is unique in this set: UNESCO explicitly calls the European bison the property’s iconic species and states that the property is home to its largest free-roaming population. The three other answer labels name distinct European parks; their own official profiles foreground mountain/lake, terraced village, and wetland/migratory-bird identities. Those distinctions explain why they are plausible same-category alternatives without claiming bison are absent there.
literalGroups.locator: UNESCO Białowieża L5, L29-L35; Lake District L42-L64 and geology L42-L54; Cinque Terre official park L415-L423 and UNESCO L47-L62; Doñana UNESCO L45-L49, L57-L60

literalGroups.literal: Это Беловежская пуща. Она сохраняет участки старовозрастного равнинного леса.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO identifies the transboundary property’s lowland old-growth forests and states that its iconic species is the European bison; it also identifies the property as containing the largest free-roaming population. This grounds both the direct answer and the forest fact.

literalGroups.literal: Лейк-Дистрикт — английский национальный парк с ледниковыми озёрами и высочайшей горой Англии.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Lake District National Park Authority says the park is in England and lists Scafell Pike first among its ten highest mountains; its geology account says glaciers and meltwater sculpted the landscape and describes its mountain/lake topography.
literalGroups.locator: Lake District facts L42-L63; geology L42-L54

literalGroups.literal: Чинкве-Терре — итальянский парк и культурный ландшафт пяти прибрежных деревень на террасированных склонах.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official Cinque Terre Park page identifies the National Park and its five hamlets and explains that terraced steep slopes supported by dry-stone walls characterize the landscape. UNESCO independently describes the five villages, coastal Ligurian setting and terraced slopes as a cultural landscape.
literalGroups.locator: Official park L415-L423; UNESCO L47-L62, especially L48-L50 and L59-L62

literalGroups.literal: Доньяна — испанский парк водно-болотных угодий у эстуария Гвадалквивира, важный для перелётных птиц.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO locates Doñana in southwestern Spain at the Guadalquivir estuary, describes marsh/wetland habitats, and says the park is internationally important for breeding, wintering and migrating birds on the East Atlantic flyway.

literalGroups.literal: Беловежская пуща — древний лес на границе Польши и Беларуси, где живёт крупнейшая свободная популяция зубров.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO locates Białowieża Forest on the Poland–Belarus border, describes the lowland old-growth forest, calls the European bison its iconic species, and identifies the largest free-roaming population of European bison there.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: Лейк-Дистрикт — английский национальный парк с ледниковыми озёрами и высочайшей горой Англии.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Grammatical and concise. “Английский национальный парк” is supported; singular “высочайшей горой” avoids the prior inaccurate plural implication. “Ледниковые озёра” is an editorial compression of the park’s lake landscape shaped by glacial processes, supported by its geology text.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Lake District is a credible alternative because it is a well-known English national park and the options are all protected European landscapes. The source’s own identity is mountains and lakes; it does not establish the European-bison association that UNESCO explicitly gives to Białowieża. I do not claim bison are absent from Lake District. The note truthfully teaches the park’s English location and its mountain/lake character.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.locator: Lake District facts L42-L63; geology L42-L54; unique key source UNESCO Białowieża L31-L35
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.fullPrompt: Какая охраняемая территория особенно известна европейским зубром?

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: Чинкве-Терре — итальянский парк и культурный ландшафт пяти прибрежных деревень на террасированных склонах.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Grammatical; the named park and apposition are clear. “Пяти прибрежных деревень” refers to the five named coastal hamlets/villages; “на террасированных склонах” describes the cultural landscape, not every village’s exact position.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Cinque Terre is a credible same-category European protected-area alternative, and UNESCO’s own description stresses its five villages and terraced Ligurian landscape. That is a distinct identifying association from Białowieża’s iconic bison. I do not assert bison are absent from Cinque Terre. The note adds a concrete, distinctive cultural-landscape fact useful for remembering the distractor.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.locator: Official Cinque Terre Park L415-L423; UNESCO L47-L62; unique key source Białowieża UNESCO L31-L35
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.fullPrompt: Какая охраняемая территория особенно известна европейским зубром?

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: Доньяна — испанский парк водно-болотных угодий у эстуария Гвадалквивира, важный для перелётных птиц.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Grammatical. “У эстуария” precisely states location at the river mouth; punctuation and participial phrase are natural.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Doñana is a credible European protected-area alternative. UNESCO foregrounds its Guadalquivir estuary, wetlands, and migratory birds, a distinctive ecological profile separate from Białowieża’s European-bison association. I do not claim bison are absent there. The note gives useful place, habitat, and bird-migration context.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.locator: Doñana UNESCO L45-L49 and L57-L60; unique key source Białowieża UNESCO L31-L35
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.fullPrompt: Какая охраняемая территория особенно известна европейским зубром?

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: Беловежская пуща — древний лес на границе Польши и Беларуси, где живёт крупнейшая свободная популяция зубров.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Grammatical and clear. “Древний лес” is a concise label for the UNESCO-described old-growth forest; “крупнейшая свободная популяция” is accurately rendered as the largest free-roaming population.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: This is the uniquely keyed option because UNESCO explicitly calls the European bison iconic to the property and says the largest free-roaming population is there. The note is truthful and useful: beyond the prompt/key, it teaches the forest’s transboundary location and bison population distinction.

correctNoteNewFact.fact: The UNESCO property crosses the Poland–Belarus border and contains the largest free-roaming European-bison population; the note’s border fact is an additional own-option fact beyond the stem/key.

absoluteDifficulty.audienceBasis: Adult general-knowledge geography/nature recognition, with a large cultural anchor: Białowieża/Belovezhskaya is an internationally recognized World Heritage forest and UNESCO itself identifies European bison as the property’s iconic species. Its name also appears in the established Russian-language song repertoire, but that song association alone is not treated as proof of bison knowledge.
absoluteDifficulty.reasoningDemand: Single-step recognition of the iconic species–protected-area association; no specialist taxonomy, numerical recall, or multistep inference is required.
absoluteDifficulty.editorialInference: The judgment that the UNESCO/iconic association is broadly recognizable to Russian-speaking adults is an editorial audience inference, not a demographic survey. The music rows are corroborating cultural visibility only; they do not establish the bison association.

limitations: The absolute EASY audience classification is an editorial inference from UNESCO’s globally recognized/explicit iconic-species association and cultural visibility; it is not based on a demographic survey.
No claim is made that European bison are absent from the three distractor parks.
